When exploring complex, unfamiliar codebases, Claude needs to examine many files and generate extensive analysis. Doing this in the main conversation would clutter the context and make subsequent development tasks less efficient. The Explore subagent handles discovery separately, then provides clean summaries to the main context.

key_concept_tested: direct execution: simple, well-scoped, single-file changes
stem: After implementing a complex user dashboard using plan mode, you need to make several follow-up changes: fix a CSS alignment issue, update a button label, add a tooltip to a form field, and change a default value in a dropdown. What's the most efficient approach?

options.label: A
options.text: Use plan mode to ensure all UI changes are coordinated properly

options.label: B
options.text: Use direct execution for each change since they're all simple, well-scoped modifications

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new plan specifically for these UI refinements

options.label: D
options.text: Use direct execution since these are simple UI tweaks to the existing implementation

explanation: These follow-up changes are all simple, well-scoped modifications to the existing dashboard: CSS fixes, text updates, tooltip additions, and default value changes. Even though there are multiple changes, each one is straightforward and doesn't require architectural decisions. Direct execution is efficient for this type of UI refinement work after the main implementation is complete.

key_concept_tested: plan mode: multiple valid approaches
stem: A developer needs to implement pagination for a data table. Instead of using plan mode to explore different approaches (client-side, server-side, infinite scroll, etc.), they immediately use direct execution saying 'Pagination is a solved problem - just implement standard server-side pagination.' What's the issue with this approach?

options.label: A
options.text: Server-side pagination might not be optimal for their specific data size and user patterns

options.label: B
options.text: Direct execution cannot implement server-side pagination correctly

options.label: C
options.text: Pagination always requires plan mode due to its complexity

options.label: D
options.text: They should have used the Explore subagent to research pagination patterns first

explanation: While pagination is a common feature, different approaches (client-side, server-side, infinite scroll, virtual scrolling) have different tradeoffs based on data size, user patterns, and performance requirements. The developer's assumption that 'standard server-side pagination' is always correct bypasses the evaluation of which approach best fits their specific context. Plan mode would allow comparing approaches and their implementation strategies.
